Latest Update: Man United transfer news: Mauricio Pochettino to use USA connection to help Red Devils 'land' defensive upgrade in January

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:38, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:41.
  • Manchester United are reportedly planning to make a move for Villarreal defender Alex Freeman when the January transfer window opens for business.
  • The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Matt Law | 23 Nov 2026 18:38, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 18:41.

Manchester United are reportedly planning to make a move for Villarreal defender Alex Freeman when the January transfer window opens for business.

The Red Devils have conceded 34 times across all competitions this season, which is the worst defensive record in Europe's top five leagues.

Man United are expected to be busy during the winter market, with at least one defender likely to arrive, while the club are also noted to be planning to sign a striker.

Centre-back has been a major problem for the 20-time English champions this season, but right-back is also an glitch, with Diogo Dalot and Noussair Mazraoui having tough campaigns.

According to Football Insider, Man United are planning to bring a new right-back to Old Trafford in January in the shape of Villarreal's Freeman.

The report claims that Man United scouts have been impressed by Freeman's level since he made the move to European football with Villarreal.

Freeman is well-known to newly introduced Red Devils head coach Mauricio Pochettino following their time together with the USA; the 22-year-old has 28 caps for his national team, scoring three goals and registering three assists in the process.

"There will be players in that US national team that Pochettino will be a big fan of," journalist Pete O'Rourke remarked on the Transfer Insider podcast.

"If he feels any player from that squad that can come in and improve the Manchester United side, then that is something he'd be foolish not to look at as well.

"There's been talk of Alex Freeman the full-back from Villarreal as being a potential target, after he has been outstanding playing in Spain.

"Obviously defence is going to be a top priority for United over the next couple of transfer windows to try and reshape the squad, and Pochettino could be key to that deal.".

Freeman started his professional career with Orlando City, making 42 appearances for the club, scoring six goals and registering seven assists, ahead of a move to Villarreal in January 2026.

The defender has one goal in 26 appearances for Villarreal, including four outings in the Champions League, while he has netted once in 17 appearances for the Yellow Submarine this season.

Freeman has a contract with Villarreal until the summer of 2032.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, chelsea transfer news: Xabi Alonso wants Barcelona right-back Jules Koundé at Chelsea and is ready to sell Marco Palestra, his £47m summer signing, to make room, according to El Nacional. The outlet indicates Alonso has pushed the case, a claim it credits to FourFourTwo, and that Palestra has Serie A interest from Juventus, AC Milan and Napoli, though it mentions no bid.

Barcelona would reportedly listen to offers of around €50m, roughly £43m, because Hansi Flick doesn’t treat Koundé as untouchable. The 28-year-old has started three of six LaLiga games this season after an ankle sprain on 17 October kept him out for over a month. El Nacional calls him a backup behind Eric García and claims he’d welcome the move.

Koundé completes 93.9% of his passes, wins 58.8% of his duels and has 58 France caps, a composed defender who could play right-back or on the right of a back three. His body is the worry: a hamstring problem in March, then an ankle injury that lingered.

Recent findings suggest that palestra won Serie A’s Defender of the Year award at Cagliari, and his 81 completed dribbles topped every defender in Europe’s top five leagues. A thigh injury delayed his Chelsea debut until October, and El Nacional puts him at 202 minutes across six matches. Alonso prefers Josh Acheampong at right-back and, per BBC Sport, uses Palestra from the bench before Malo Gusto. He scored once in 37 league games, and his crossing remains modest.

Sources indicate that not as a swap. Palestra is a wing-back who beats opponents on the outside, while Koundé is a passer and cover defender best placed on the right of three centre-backs. Selling one doesn’t remove the need for the other, and Chelsea’s real shortage is right-sided cover: Reece James is injured and has been used in midfield, and Acheampong, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back.

Industry observers note that koundé would solve that, but Gusto is the sale to make. He has lost his place, is reportedly open to a January exit, and Chelsea priced him at £75m in June, so even a discounted fee would cover much of Koundé’s £43m.

Sources indicate that selling Palestra after 202 minutes would mean writing off a player Alonso recruited and noted needs time to adapt, to buy a 28-year-old with a muscle-injury record. Chelsea were fifth, 11 points behind Arsenal, before Leeds visited, without European football. Buy Koundé if the medical is clean, sell Gusto and keep Palestra.

Rangers must find their shooting boots quicker to prevent the need to dig themselves out of needless holes

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1273 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.
  • Sources indicate that that’s fair enough.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 12:52 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 13:26 EST, 22 November 2026.

Derek McInnes chose to dress up the poor level of chance conversion from his Rangers side as something for those insistent on dwelling on the negatives at the end of a last-gasp win over Motherwell.

Sources indicate that that’s fair enough. He wants to keep the energy up. He wants to place the focus, instead, on a 13-game unbeaten run. He wants to make more of the fact his team are capable of digging in and getting wins over the line by hook or by crook even when it isn’t going exactly to plan.

Recent findings suggest that it’s a form of motivation, and motivating people doesn’t always come through hammering on about their deficiencies. The truth is this, though: you really shouldn’t be needing a scrappy 88th-minute winner courtesy of a couple of jammy deflections in a game which has seen you deliver 29 shots on goal with 11 of those on target.

Yes, Motherwell keeper Alex Paulsen had a good night. One double save from substitute Findlay Curtis and Dujon Sterling in the 85th minute was quite exceptional. This, however, wasn’t quite the superhuman display from the Kiwi that many were making it out to be.

A lot of the saves he made were straightforward. Too often, Rangers blazed efforts high and wide. They dominated the first quarter of this game until Jake Girdwood-Reich cancelled out Manny Fernandez’s early opener, lost their rhythm a bit, as they are wont to do, and then ran the show completely in the second half.

They should have won by a country mile and it is necessary to look into why they didn’t.

Ryan Naderi rejoices in scoring Rangers' late winner against Motherwell.

Emmanuel Fernandez broke the deadlock on eight minutes at Fir Park.

According to recent reports, mcInnes was justified in being happy with many aspects of his side’s performance at Fir Park. Ryan Naderi did put in a strong display as he spearheaded the frontline, although he did miss two gilt-edged chances before settling it late on with an untidy effort that deflected off Martin Moormann — who had already blocked a Badredine Bouanani shot — and landed in the net.

The Czech international is developing a reputation for key goals that are getting Rangers out of the mire — and keeping them in contention for the title — but McInnes needs infinitely more in terms of numbers from those around him.

Not xG or pass completion or any of those niche interests. Goals and assists is what we’re talking about here. The stuff that really changes games and puts points on the board.

In a recent development, first in the dock on this front, talented individuals that really need to be held to account, are attackers Minsu Kim and Bouanani. Listen, McInnes has already spoken plenty on the need for both of them to deliver more in those key metrics. He obviously doesn’t want to come across as a stuck record.

It has been revealed that both players are technically proficient. They are exciting. The view from this vantage point is that they very definitely do have it in them to be gamechangers, but they’re starting to get a little bit annoying now.

Thanks to the corner that set up Fernandez for the opening goal, Minsu, who started in a more central role with Kevin Kelsy being benched, does have one assist on the board finally. That’s a pretty grim return, though, from 15 appearances.

Particularly worrying from the South Korean was his reaction when presented with a golden opportunity to break his scoring duck just before the hour. Naderi teed him up perfectly with a pass to the left. Minsu had time to control the ball and pick his spot.

His sclaffed effort, easily saved by Paulsen at the near post, was atrocious. It reeked of a guy short of confidence in the final third and growing progressively more anxious about getting his name on the scoresheet. Maybe he’s just trying too hard, but he needs to get the finger out, keep the mind calm and start taking the heat off the likes of Naderi and Kelsy with some major contributions.

Same goes for Bouanani. His late effort did, at least, lead to Naderi’s winner, albeit more through accident than design, but his record reads one goal and one assist in 10 appearances. He’s a dangerous, tricky winger. He beats people for fun. He should be doing more than this.

Djeidi Gassama, a more limited player than Minsu or Bouanani, started against Motherwell and does have five assists to his name, but he’s only managed one goal, in a 5-1 League Cup rout of St Mirren.

Meanwhile, Findlay Curtis has no goals and no assists from 15 outings, although only five of those have been first-team starts.

Recent findings suggest that that’s four blokes who play along the frontline and they’ve managed two goals between them. You do the maths on that.

Derek McInnes was delighted at full-time but Rangers should have won with more comfort.

There are others throughout the team, though, who can be doing more to make life easier from a goalscoring perspective.

Fernandez confirmed himself as a real threat from set-pieces last season. He’s a real weapon in the air. Saturday’s goal was his first this term. Rangers need to do better at harnessing what he brings in an attacking context from dead-ball situations.

Industry observers note that A few more in the way of goal interventions from midfield would be welcome, too. Dan Neil can finish. He revealed that with those two spectacular goals against Celtic in the 3-0 Premier Sports Cup win at Ibrox in September.

According to recent reports, in his 17 other outings outwith that match, however, he has only scored once and delivered one assist. He had a brilliant chance at Fir Park just after the interval and slid it wide of the far post.

Nico Raskin, meanwhile, has one goal and no assists to his name.

In a recent development, he put one great chance from a header wide in the second half. Then he blazed over from a promising position after releasing Bouanani out wide with a super diagonal ball and running a ridiculous distance to latch onto the return.

McInnes insists he’s never seen a squad practise crossing and shooting like this one. However much they are doing in training at Auchenhowie, they need to bring it to matchdays.

Everything is there for Rangers this season. There are definitely promising signs in their overall play while Celtic, of course, are poorly run from a footballing perspective with an OAP manager, and a fanbase in open revolt against the board.

Rangers now have a run of six games from eight at home that could — and should — be a real platform for a serious title bid.

They just have to wake up to the fact that depending on Naderi to drag them out of a hole and drag them over the line again and again and again is simply not a sustainable way of working.

Rangers (4-2-3-1): Pandur 7; Sterling 7, Fernandez 7, Makhanya 6, Rommens 6; Raskin 7, Neil 6.5 (Chukwuani 86); Bouanani 7, Minsu 6.5 (Curtis 78), Gassama 6 (Kelsy 69); Naderi 7.5. Booked: Naderi. Manager: Derek McInnes 7.

  • Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Liverpool transfer news: Liverpool are tracking Borussia Dortmund left-back Daniel Svensson, according to fussball-news.de, which names them and Arsenal as the most interested clubs.

Manchester United, Leeds, Milan, Juventus, Inter and Real Madrid are also watching the 24-year-old. Liverpool and Milan are reportedly preparing concrete steps for the winter window, although the report attributes no bid to either.

Dortmund will not make it easy. They want to keep a player contracted until June 2029 and plan to raise his salary, while Svensson feels settled and has no wish for a rushed move. A sale would cost at least €45m (about £38m), and Premier League clubs are ready to test Dortmund with a €30m (roughly £25m) offer, yet FotMob values him at just €23m.

The numbers explain the interest. Svensson has started all 10 Bundesliga games this season. His expected assists total of 1.13 comes without a single assist, and he has made 22 tackles, 14 interceptions and 45 recoveries while passing at 86.1%. He can play in midfield.

The flaws are clear. He has won only eight of 29 aerial duels and landed six of 32 crosses. He also plays as a wing-back in front of a back three, so Andoni Iraola’s back four would ask him to defend more of the flank alone.

In a recent development, iraola’s 4-2-3-1 sends full-backs forward, and Milos Kerkez, bought for a reported £40m last year, has no goals or assists in the Premier League this season. Kostas Tsimikas, 30, is the backup on a contract that expires next year.

Not in January, and not at €45m. A €30m offer would fail, and £38m for a player FotMob values at €23m is poor business. Summer 2027 is the realistic window, once Tsimikas’s deal has run down.

Sources indicate that the bigger problem sits on the other flank. Ronald Araujo, a centre-back by trade, is filling in at right-back while injuries have hit that position all season, so Iraola needs a natural right-back more urgently than a second left-back. Kerkez is 22 and signed until 2030, so Svensson would challenge him rather than replace him, which is healthy given Kerkez’s lack of end product.

Industry observers note that kerkez arrived with two Premier League seasons behind him, while Svensson would have to adapt to a new league and a new system. Liverpool should buy a right-back first and hold a ceiling of around £35m for Svensson, because above that they would repeat the Kerkez gamble with less evidence.

What do various cancers have in common?

📅 24 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (604 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
  • Get Nature+, our best-value online-access subscription.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, cancers arising in distinct organs differ in their cellular organization, genetic alterations and patterns of how they progress1. Now, a large-scale analysis reveals striking similarities between the non-malignant cells found in the tumour microenvironment (TME) — the local environment in and around a tumour, in which non-malignant cells interact with cancer cells — across various types of cancer. Writing in Nature, Januszyk et al.2 integrate single-cell data from 42 types of tumour in humans and mice. The authors identify recurring patterns of gene activity in immune cells and in stromal cells, which contribute to tissue structure and function. These similarities provide a starting point for testing whether treatments directed at the non-cancerous cells of the TME might be effective across a range of cancer types.

Frosinone head coach Massimiliano Alvini has admitted that his side simply gave AC Milan too many opportunities.

Industry observers note that it has been a very positive return to the top flight for Frosinone so far, given that a point last night at San Siro would have seen them move back into the European places. However, they were ultimately given a bit of a humbling by Milan, who won 5-1 thanks to a ruthless counter-attacking display.

Some have questioned if the Canarini were a bit too aggressive in their approach to the game, given they played with such a high line and allowed space for Adrien Rabiot, Diego Moreira, Goncalo Ramos, Ardon Jashari, Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic to exploit.

Industry observers note that alvini was present in the press conference room at San Siro after the full-time whistle and he analysed what was perhaps the most difficult night of the season for his team. MilanNews transcribed his assessments.

Should the game have been played differently?

Recent findings suggest that “Frosinone played their game but made a few mistakes they don’t usually make, but that’s certainly not my concern, losing by such a large margin. What’s worrying are the mistakes we made that we could have avoided.”.

“We made a mistake on the first goal, which was a mistake of our own, while the other goals we conceded were goals we absolutely could have avoided. We conceded them and were naive.

“It’s a mistake of our own, and so today, from this perspective, if you come to Milan against Milan and make these mistakes, it’s only natural that we end up losing like this, by such a large scoreline.

“That’s the analysis, even though I think the scoreline is even too large: the first half, in my opinion, was extraordinary on our part.”.

Did the absences have an impact, forcing you to experiment a bit?

In a recent development, “There’s nothing experimental about it. We played with the same principles, running forward to get to Rabiot. We preferred to bring on a defender who would push forward rather than a midfielder.

“In my opinion, this definitely didn’t influence the result, but rather the attitude, the idea, or the match strategy. And we certainly made – as I remarked before and I’ll repeat – mistakes we don’t usually make.

“If you give Milan certain chances, with such strong players and the quality of this team, you risk losing, and that’s what happened. You risk losing with a heavy defeat, and that’s what happened.

“He had a problem with that back heel in the box, and he definitely needs tests. It’s too early now; we’ll have to wait for the tests, which will be done starting Tuesday, but it’s definitely a problem.”.

According to recent reports, “We had a chance with Monterisi after a minute, we hit the post, and we created a lot. I have nothing to say to the team for their attitude and the way they played.

Sources indicate that “We, I repeat, made some naivety, some mistakes. It’s also up to me to understand that there are notable players on the other side who can cause problems.”.

“It’s a result that definitely needs to be managed, navigated, and channeled, but it doesn’t change my attitude at all. We have 20 points today. The path we need to take is to try to stay in Serie A, and we’ll try to do so with this attitude, with this identity: this is the path we’ll take.

In a recent development, “Four years ago, I drew a game against Milan by playing defensively, and we took home a point. Today we made some mistakes, but this is the path we’ll take. I’m happier with the management, with the team’s identity, to try to achieve that objective, and this is what we’ll continue to do.”.

Atletico Madrid will be bidding to return to winning ways in the Champions League when they continue their league stage campaign against Viking FK on Wednesday night.

This match will represent the first-ever contest between Atletico and Viking, although the Spanish team have won six of their seven previous meetings against Norwegian clubs.

Atletico boast a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's Champions League league stage, with the result leaving them 23rd in the overall table on four points.

Diego Simeone's side opened their league stage campaign with a 2-1 defeat to Liverpool before beating Manchester United and then drawing with Stuttgart, but they suffered a 2-0 home defeat to Bayern Munich in their last fixture in the competition.

Atletico have European games against PSV Eindhoven, Bodo/Glimt and Fenerbahce to come after this one, and it would be a major shock if they were not present in the knockout round of the tournament.

The Red and Whites will enter this match off the back of a 3-0 win over Getafe in Spain's top flight, with the result leaving them third in the La Liga table on 31 points, five points behind leaders Barcelona.

Atletico lost 2-1 on aggregate to Arsenal in last season's Champions League semi-finals, and they have been runners-up in this tournament on two occasions (2014 and 2016).

Viking, meanwhile, have a record of one win, one draw and two defeats from their four matches in this season's league stage, and they actually sit above Atletico in the table (22nd).

The Eliteserien champions lost their section opener to Stuttgart before claiming a point in a 3-3 draw with Bayern Munich, but they were then beaten by Aston Villa at Villa Park.

The Dark Blues did have a huge European win last time out, though, recording a 4-1 victory over Sabah, which gave their hopes of qualification a huge boost.

Viking, who are jointly-managed by Bjarte Lunde Aarsheim and Morten Jensen, are playing in the Champions League for the first time since 1992-93, when they were beaten by Barcelona in the first round.

The Norwegian outfit have scored in their last 12 European matches, which is a club record, while none of Atletico's last 42 Champions League fixtures have finished goalless.

Pochettino’s trust is a real advantage, since he knows exactly what work rate he gets, but trust doesn’t turn a 28-year-old with one league goal this season into a £28m solution to a defensive crisis. Juventus also just rewarded him with a contract to 2030, so they have no reason to sell cheaply.

Romano mentioned Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in the same breath, and each offers more control from midfield. If Pochettino wants a familiar face, a rotation option on a short deal makes sense. Spending about £28m on a runner does not.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it said in its October economic review.
  • The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.
  • India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

India's Ministry of Finance expects India's economy to grow at a pace of 7.3% in the current fiscal year based on its latest assessment of current data, it said in its October economic review.

The estimate is a slight increase on the previous forecast of 7.1%.

India's current fiscal year, known as FY27, runs from April 1, 2026 to March 31, 2027.

The report contrasted these figures with global growth predictions of nearer 3%, saying "India's growth momentum, by comparison, has held firm.".

The ministry noted growth in various key indicators like energy consumption, port traffic, goods and services tax (GST) collections, and car sales had accelerated in the previous quarter.

However, the ministry also warned of continued inflationary pressure and pressure on the rupee currency, as well as downside risks from the El Nino weather phonemenon that could threaten soil moisture ahead of the winter sowing season.

It stated that external factors like oil prices and "global uncertainties" — seemingly a reference at least in part to the instablity in the Middle East — continued to pressure the rupee's value and pose inflationary risks.

Consumer price inflation (CPI), the wholesale price index (WPI), food cost prices and fuel and power prices were all rising month for month, albeit at very different rates.

Sources indicate that the CPI was up 5.54% year-on-year in September, but the WPI had risen more sharply at 11.39%. Food index inflation was up by 8% in rural areas, and a slightly more modest 7.18% in urban centers.

But, as in many other countries, fuel and power costs increases were in an entirely different league, at 25.85% inflation in September 2026 comapred to the same month a year earlier, prior to the outbreak of fighting in the Middle East.

Although it has been a comparatively slow decline, the rupee has been consistently losing value against the US dollar over the past five years, threatening the country's relative purchasing power internationally. This slide has picked up pace in the last 15 months or so.

But the ministry pointed to foreign exchange reserves worth some $721 billion and said that India was "well-positioned" to weather such risks and sustain its expansionary trajectory..

Tottenham transfer news: Tottenham Hotspur are one of four clubs tracking Hakan Calhanoglu, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Italian outlet lists Galatasaray, Juventus and Como alongside Spurs, although it gives no detail on how far Tottenham’s interest has progressed.

Industry observers note that the timing matters because the Inter midfielder’s contract expires on 30 June 2027, which lets him agree a pre-contract with a foreign club from January. Inter want to extend but are trimming wages for their over-30s. Calhanoglu earns roughly £5.7m a year, and Inter are discussing £4.4m plus bonuses. He prefers to stay but hopes to avoid a heavy cut, and no formal offer exists yet.

According to recent reports, calhanoglu turns 33 in February. FotMob shows three goals in 485 minutes from nine Serie A appearances, 91.4% pass accuracy, 20 chances created and a 98th-percentile ranking for shot attempts among Serie A central midfielders.

Passing range, long-distance shooting and dead-ball quality remain his strengths. He wins only 44.4% of his duels, though, completes a quarter of his dribbles, and his recovery speed will keep dropping with age. FotMob values him at about £6.4m, down from a £39m peak in 2024.

Industry observers note that roberto De Zerbi wants his midfield to dictate play from deep, which suits Calhanoglu’s skills. Spurs have 15 points from 11 league games after beating Ipswich 2-0 on Saturday, their fourth win in five. Yet Sandro Tonali (£100m) and Mateus Fernandes (£85m) joined in July, and Rodrigo Bentancur, Conor Gallagher and Archie Gray compete for the same places.

Sources indicate that not as a priority. Money isn’t the obstacle. Tonali reportedly earns more than £275,000 a week, so Calhanoglu’s wages would barely register, and a free transfer costs no fee. Squad space is the problem. Spurs bought Tonali and Fernandes to run De Zerbi’s base for years, and a 33-year-old in the same role would either sit on the bench or take minutes from Gray and Lucas Bergvall, whom the club needs to develop.

Industry observers note that spurs would also struggle to sell the project without European football, while Galatasaray can reportedly offer higher wages. The case only strengthens if Tonali or Bentancur leaves, or if De Zerbi wants a penalty and set-piece specialist. Neither applies now, and nothing forces Spurs to act in January.

Calhanoglu’s output is real, but it comes with a decline in athleticism that a 33-year-old can’t reverse. Spurs would be paying for a short-term fix in a position where they have already invested £185m in the long-term answer.

Liverpool’s £400m front line clicks but win at Brentford turns on red card

📅 17 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 25 min read (5033 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~25 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction.
  • It has been revealed that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk.
  • It has been revealed that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Only time will tell if Liverpool’s £400m front line can ever justify the extraordinary amount of money that was spent on them, but this was at least a significant step in the right direction. In a gritty victory away to Brentford, all four of Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz, Bradley Barcola and Victor Muñoz either scored or assisted goals.

It has been revealed that admittedly, the task was made significantly easier by the major turning point of this game: a red card for Brentford’s Yehor Yarmoliuk. At the time of Yarmoliuk’s “headbutting action” towards Liverpool defender Jeremy Jacquet, the visitors were trailing 1-0 and looking worryingly short of ideas in attack.

It has been revealed that but as the context of the match changed, so did the level of threat from the visitors. Against 10 men, with more space in which to operate, Liverpool’s forwards looked increasingly dangerous. Wirtz began to pull the strings, Barcola started to cause problems, Muñoz stretched the Brentford defence and Isak became a lurking menace.

For Andoni Iraola, who had failed to beat Brentford in six attempts as manager of Bournemouth, it would have made for an immensely pleasing sight. After last weekend’s thrashing by Manchester City, Liverpool have responded with a 6-3 Champions League win over LASK and this victory against a previously unbeaten Brentford. Iraola will know, however, that his team’s numerical advantage was the fundamental reason for the dramatic shift in the flow of this game.

It has been revealed that the Gtech Community Stadium simmered with outrage following Yarmoliuk’s red card, which came in the eighth minute of first-half stoppage time, and the home fans probably had a point. Yes, there was a movement of the midfielder’s head towards Jacquet, but it was hardly an act of violence. Jacquet’s reaction, collapsing to the turf in mock agony, was embarrassing but predictably effective. Cynics would say the Frenchman changed the game for his team. Purists would argue this is no way in which to influence a match.

Recent findings suggest that keith Andrews, the Brentford head coach, chose against complaining too aggressively. But he did make it clear what he thought of Jacquet’s behaviour. “I do think they were cute and clever,” Andrews stated. “He is walking into Yarmo. But we need to look at ourselves and I understand why it was a red. Yarmo is an amazing young man and he will learn from this.”.

In a recent development, brentford had been the better team before this decisive incident and they deserved their lead, given to them by a majestic header by Keane Lewis-Potter, from Igor Thiago’s cross. It was a moment of attacking quality that Iraola’s glitzy attackers had looked unlikely to replicate, especially when Barcola fluffed a one-versus-one showdown with Brentford goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher.

To play an entire half of Premier League football with only 10 men is a brutal examination, though, and Brentford were unable to pass the test. Wirtz unleashed Muñoz after an hour, allowing the Spaniard to fire home with his left foot, before Barcola’s header found Isak in the box with 20 minutes remaining.

It was Isak’s fifth goal of the campaign, which means he has now beaten last season’s tally of four. He has scored in all five of his Premier League appearances against Brentford. “I didn’t have too many chances,” Isak noted. “I was waiting for my moment.”.

Any hopes of a Brentford comeback evaporated in stoppage time, when the home side lost another man to a red card. This time it was Vitaly Janelt, who received his second yellow for fouling Rio Ngumoha, Liverpool’s sparkling teenage winger. From there, Liverpool’s attempts to score a third were comically poor. “We lacked some composure,” admitted Iraola. “But it was a good battle today, and very vital points for us. To take three points here is very valuable.”.

An encouraging result for Liverpool, then, but this was not an afternoon without concerns. The first-half showing was worrying, and there were also injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai and Jeremie Frimpong. Both players limped off, and Iraola remarked they will now be out “for some time”.

In a recent development, the loss of Szoboszlai will be a particular concern, as he was rushed back from a hamstring injury for this game but then felt the same muscle again after only 32 minutes of action. “It’s a very delicate situation,” stated Iraola.

The injury to Frimpong meant that Muñoz, a winger, played most of the second half as an attack-minded right-back. He did so excellently, and took his goal with impressive composure after Wirtz had pushed the ball into his path. Liverpool’s second was similarly clinical, as Isak pounced on Barcola’s knock-down in a congested penalty area. These, clearly, are the moments of game-changing quality that Liverpool expect from their big-money forwards. Iraola will hope it was a sign of things to come.

Industry observers note that good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the 3pm kick-offs. Manchester City burst the Anfield bubble last weekend but were defeated by Paris St-Germain in a Champions League thriller on Wednesday, and Enzo Maresca will have to manage his leading cast members’ workload. Before Ipswich Town’s visit to the Etihad he floated the idea of resting some of his players at some point.

“We are thinking about this not just with Erling [Haaland] because we have players, unfortunately or fortunately, they are playing all the games with us and all the games with the international teams,” Maresca stated in his pre-match press conference.”.

“Elliot [Anderson], Enzo [Fernández], Marc [Guéhi], Erling, Rúben [Dias] – so at some point we probably need to give them some rest.”.

Recent findings suggest that ipswich’s spirited start to the season was characterised by a stunning late turnaround against Fulham last weekend. Gary O’Neil’s side have accrued three wins in their first six top-flight matches for the first time since 1993 and may consider today’s match as something of a free hit.

Elsewhere, Liverpool’s confidence-building midweek win in Austria was underlined by Bradley Barcola’s first, second and third goals for the club. It was exactly what the France winger needed, and with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo emerging as doubts for this afternoon’s trip to Brentford, the attacking burden may fall on Barcola and Florian Wirtz’s shoulders once more.

Sources indicate that breaking down fourth-placed Brentford, who are one of only three teams to remain undefeated this season, will be a tall task. Keith Andrews’ stock has never been higher, but the same cannot be stated for Álvaro Arbeloa, whose winless Fulham are bottom of the league.

According to recent reports, pressure was already mounting before Fulham’s three-game run against the promoted teams, and the late collapse at Portman Road will not have helped the Spaniard’s cause. Defeat by Hull City will not be seen kindly by the club’s hierarchy.

Manchester City’s £31m left-back wanted in Turin: Loan or sale in January?

📅 05 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (430 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Footballtransfertavern

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that calcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen.
  • In a recent development, city want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement.
  • Sources indicate that city paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that calcioMercato reports that Juventus have started monitoring Rayan Aït-Nouri ahead of the transfer market reopening, and the Manchester City left-back seems ready to listen. The Algeria international wants to restart his career elsewhere, views Turin favourably and has told his entourage to strengthen contacts, while the interest from Juventus is real and the club intends to act soon to test the deal’s feasibility.

In a recent development, city want to sell outright and reinvest immediately, whereas Juventus prefer a loan with an option to buy, which suits a club bound by a UEFA settlement agreement. They first asked in August and City refused, while Gazzetta dello Sport says Luciano Spalletti wants competition for Andrea Cambiaso.

Sources indicate that city paid Wolves a reported £31m in June 2025 and gave him a contract until 2030, yet Enzo Maresca reportedly ranks the 25-year-old behind Joško Gvardiol and Nico O’Reilly. He had played 168 minutes in all competitions by mid-November, none of them in the Premier League, and his only starts have come in the EFL Cup.

It has been revealed that his strengths explain the fee. Aït-Nouri scored nine goals and set up 15 in 135 Premier League games for Wolves, added five assists in 1,605 minutes last season, and can also operate in central areas.

Sources indicate that the weakness is defensive security, because he is an ultra-attacking left-back. That matters now, with City on one point from their last four league games after losing 3-1 at Nottingham Forest and drawing 1-1 with Fulham on Saturday.

No, not in January, and not on terms that leave City carrying all the risk. Maresca has used Nico O’Reilly in midfield this season, yet O’Reilly started only seven of City’s first 15 games while managing a back problem, so an available specialist left-back is no luxury. Khusanov, Nunes and Guéhi all picked up knocks at Forest, which leaves the back line short.

In a recent development, city should treat the Juventus talks as a pricing exercise. A straight loan sends a 25-year-old on a contract until 2030 away for six months and returns him no more valuable, so only a loan with an obligation to buy close to the £31m fee makes sense.

According to recent reports, otherwise, give him a league start, see whether his attacking threat helps a side that keeps conceding, and let Maresca’s evidence decide. A club that paid £31m for a left-back last year has not shown he cannot do the job; it has shown only that the manager prefers somebody else.

  • The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 23 Nov 2026 19:39, Last updated: 23 Nov 2026 19:39.

Hibernian FC host Dundee FC in the Scottish Premiership at Easter Road Stadium on Tuesday.

The fixture was moved from October 31 because of Hibernian's Premier Sports Cup semi-final, and both clubs arrive after heavy defeats on November 21, with Hibernian beaten 4-0 at home by Dundee United and Dundee thrashed 8-0 by Heart of Midlothian at Dens Park.

Marink Reedijk's Hibernian sit 11th in the Scottish Premiership table with 11 points from 13 games, a return of three wins, two draws and eight defeats, and their goal difference of minus six is the product of 15 goals scored and 21 conceded.

The Hibees are the only club in the division yet to win a league match at home this season, and they have conceded 15 goals in seven league games at Easter Road.

Dundee United made that record worse on Saturday, with Zac Sapsford scoring from the rebound after Raphael Sallinger saved his sixth-minute penalty, adding a second before half time, and Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall completing a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's heaviest home defeat to United.

Reedijk was appointed on September 24 after David Gray was sacked, and he lost his first three league games in charge, 1-0 at Dundee United on October 10 and 2-1 at home to both Falkirk on October 17 and Celtic on October 25.

The cup has been kinder, as goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath beat Heart of Midlothian 2-1 at Hampden Park on November 1, Hibernian's first win over their city rivals at the national stadium after four defeats there, and set up a Premier Sports Cup final against Rangers on Sunday, December 13.

McGrath then struck a 25-yard shot just before the hour at Pittodrie on November 7, and substitutes Callum Wright, Nicky Cadden and Thibault Klidje added the rest in a 4-0 win that was Hibernian's biggest at Aberdeen since 1968 and remains Reedijk's only league victory.

Joe Newell, who wore the captain's armband against United in place of the injured Felix Passlack, spoke afterwards of the players' shame and embarrassment, and the midfielder will know that Tuesday offers the first chance to answer it in front of the Easter Road crowd.

Steven Pressley's Dundee sit seventh with 17 points from 13 games, a record of five wins, two draws and six defeats that leaves them six points and four places above Hibernian, with 18 goals scored and 23 conceded.

The Dee had conceded only 15 times in their first 12 league games and collected five wins in that run, with Owen Goodman playing every minute in goal and keeping two clean sheets.

That solidity vanished on Saturday, when Hearts led 4-0 at half time and Owen Bevan was sent off on 56 minutes for a foul on Claudio Braga, with the visitors winning 8-0 in what The Courier described as Dundee's worst-ever defeat at Dens Park.

Pressley took responsibility for the display afterwards, while pundit Richard Foster argued the players must also own a result that was Hearts' biggest top-flight win since 1957.

The defeat came a fortnight after a 2-1 loss at St Johnstone on November 7, and it ended an unbeaten home run of four league games for a side that had collected the bulk of its points at Dens Park.

Dundee will also remember that Hibernian won the first meeting 2-1 at Dens Park on August 30, and Tuesday is the second of three league games between the sides before the split.

Bradley Fink and Joe Westley share the Dundee scoring lead with four league goals each, and Westley, who takes the penalties, came off the bench to equalise at St Johnstone within two minutes of the restart.

Hibernian Scottish Premiership form:.

Hibernian form (all competitions):.

Dundee Scottish Premiership form:.

Dundee form (all competitions):.

Passlack, who took the captaincy from Boyle after Reedijk's arrival, is out with a hamstring injury sustained in the eighth minute at Aberdeen, and Reedijk has refused to put a date on his return as the defender races to be fit for the Rangers final.

Alex Williams replaced Passlack at Pittodrie and made his first start against United, so he is the likely right-back again.

Grant Hanley is out after thumb surgery, Adam Mayor has a hamstring problem, and on-loan Stoke City striker Nathan Lowe has a stress fracture that Reedijk will assess week by week.

Kanayo Megwa remains sidelined with a thigh problem and Rocky Bushiri is still recovering from the Achilles injury he suffered in May.

Left-back Jordan Obita is back in contention after a calf injury, and on-loan Manchester United midfielder Jacob Devaney returned from international duty with Ireland, giving Reedijk extra options if he rings the changes.

Owen Elding, 20, leads the line in Lowe's absence, with Boyle and McGrath operating around him as they did in the Hampden semi-final.

For the visitors, Bevan serves the first of a two-match ban after his straight red card against Hearts, ruling him out at Easter Road and at Aberdeen on Saturday, November 28.

Joe Wright, who was on the bench against Hearts, is the natural replacement alongside Ryan Astley, but he has played little league football this season.

Simon Murray, Finlay Robertson and Jack Moorhouse are all out for the season with anterior cruciate ligament injuries.

Bobby Wales, the on-loan striker, is still recovering from an ankle injury.

Goodman, beaten eight times at Dens Park, is expected to keep his place in goal.

Hibernian possible starting lineup:.

Sallinger; Williams, Kerr, Ivezic, Iredale; Chaiwa, Newell; McGrath, Mulligan, Boyle; Elding.

Dundee possible starting lineup:.

Goodman; D. Wright, Astley, J. Wright, Samuels; Forrest, Hamilton, Finnigan, Reilly; Westley, Fink.

Hibernian have not won a league game at Easter Road all season and have shipped 15 goals in seven home matches, and a side that has just lost 4-0 to United at home is unlikely to turn that around in three days against opponents who beat them at Dens Park on August 30.

Dundee arrive without Bevan and with the memory of an 8-0 defeat, and a makeshift centre-back pairing facing Elding and Boyle will struggle to hold a clean sheet.

The counter-argument is that Pittodrie remains Reedijk's only league win, but Dundee's points have come overwhelmingly at Dens Park, and their goal difference of minus five is the worst in the top eight, which is why a Hibernian goal looks likelier than a clean sheet for either side.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Company, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

For Star Trek fans, he was the legendary Captain Picard; the British actor and director Patrick Stewart, longtime member of the  Royal Shakespeare Company, died on Thursday at the age of 86 following a "brief and poignant journey" with Alzheimer's disease and Lewy body dementia, according to an official statement on his social media accounts.

In Los Angeles, California, far away from the small English village of Mirfield where he was born, Stewart achieved world fame. He was 47 years old when he landed the role of a lifetime in the legendary science fiction series Star Trek: Playing Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek: The Next Generation," he stepped into the shoes of the legendary Captain James T. Kirk, played by William Shatner.

Stewart brought a calm, measured and distinctly British presence that rapidly made Picard a fan favorite and a cult figure in the Star Trek universe. He returned to the role decades later in the spin-off series "Star Trek: Picard," which ended in 2023, proving the character's enduring appeal.

As Captain Jean-Luc Picard, he led the crew of the starship Enterprise, a spaceship with the sizeable mission: "To explore strange new worlds. To seek out new life and new civilizations" — and most importantly, "to boldly go where no man has gone before!".

It has been revealed that stewart's interest in acting was sparked in the early 1950s when a teacher asked him to recite a work by Shakespeare. His passion for Shakespeare stayed with him until the end.

Recent findings suggest that his parents were far removed from the glamor of the theatrical world. His father was a highly respected officer in the British Army during World War II, but at home, he was an abusive husband, and young Patrick had to helplessly witness repeated violence against his mother. Stewart wrote about his experiences with domestic violence in The Guardian in 2009. The stage, he confessed there, seemed to him "a far safer place" than reality; he saw acting as a way to escape his home life.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that patrick began acting at the age of 12. At 16, he left school early and, thanks to a scholarship, studied acting in Bristol, England. Along the way, he worked as a journalist. In 1965, he became an official member of the Royal Shakespeare Manufacturer, and remained with the theather company from 1966 to 1982. Such was his passion for the great English playwright and lyricist that he even shared his sonnets on his Twitter account during the 2020 coronavirus pandemic.

According to recent reports, stewart dazzled the theater world with his own stage adaptation of Charles Dickens' 1843 tale "A Christmas Carol." He played more than 30 roles himself. After its 1987 premiere in Stewart's hometown of Mirfield, the one-man show became a critics' favorite and a long-running hit on Broadway in New York.

In a recent development, in the same year,  Stewart went from being a stage actor to an international TV star. Star Trek producer Robert Justman offered him the role of Captain Jean-Luc Picard, one of the main characters in a upcoming edition of the popular TV series "Star Trek: The Next Generation.".

The successful Shakespearean hesitated. Until then, he had never worked in Hollywood. But his agent encouraged him to accept the role, Stewart recalled in a 2020 interview with the German newspaper Die Welt. "You can accept the offer as a start for now. It won't be a major deal, you can't revive a series as iconic as Star Trek anyway.".

But his agent was to be proven wrong: Stewart led the Starship Enterprise through its galactic adventures for seven seasons and four full-length feature films. The TV series had astronomical success on Earth in a very short time. At first, the producers were at odds as to whether Stewart's British accent could really fit the role of commander of a US starship in the 24th century, but it soon became impossible to imagine the series without the subtly diplomatic Captain Picard, who often quoted Shakespeare while at the helm. It seemed as if all the time he had spent as a Shakespearean actor had prepared him to command the Enterprise, Stewart once remarked with a wink. When the cult series ended in 1994, he had ruled out ever returning to the Enterprise's command center.

Sources indicate that in 2010, the actor was knighted by the Queen of England. Stewart considered it the greatest honor of his career to stand alongside acting greats such as Sir Laurence Olivier and Sir Alec Guinness.

Industry observers note that beyond the screen, Stewart has long used his voice for social and human rights causes. In recent years, he has drawn attention to issues such as violence against women, age discrimination and the protection of children.

Recent findings suggest that in a June 2020 interview, "Playboy" asked the Fresh York resident whether he was considering retiring from acting. "Never! That would mean giving up my life," replied Stewart, who was approaching his 80th birthday at the time. He was filming the second of three seasons of "Star Trek: Picard." The series ends with a final episode in which the retired Starfleet admiral makes his last appearance. In the series, Picard retires to his family vineyard in France but is drawn back into space to confront new threats to the Federation.

Sources indicate that this series also showcases Stewart's affection for his pit bull, Ginger. In "Star Trek: Picard," Picard also has a pit bull, a loyal four-legged companion named Number One — a deliberate reference to Stewart's real-life love of the breed. For his efforts to combat prejudice against pit bulls and to support their adoption, Stewart was honored by the US animal welfare organization ASPCA, among others.

In 2024, he published his memoir "Making it So." In it, he recounts his passion for theater and his love of Shakespeare.

Recent findings suggest that now, at the age of 86, the British actor has finally departed for another galaxy. Farewell, Patrick Stewart!

The point leaves Fiorentina 15th in the table on 9 points.

Sources indicate that the hosts led after four minutes. Mateo Pellegrino scored, set up by Pedro Goncalves. Nick Woltemade levelled in the 32nd minute from a Randal Kolo Muani assist, and it was 1-1 at half-time.

Industry observers note that fiorentina went ahead again in the 54th minute. Guglielmo Vicario made the first save, but the Juventus defenders were too slow to clear. Alieu Njie forced in the rebound. Bremer then reached a Douglas Luiz corner in the six-yard box before David de Gea could get to it.

Juventus completed 384 accurate passes to Fiorentina’s 273. Fiorentina still attempted 22 shots to Juventus’s 18, and both sides had 6 on target. The expected goals figures, 2.46 for Juventus and 2.14 for Fiorentina, are consistent with a fairly even contest despite the visitors’ control of the ball.

The closing stages could have gone either way. Former Juventus defender Radu Drăgușin headed in from a corner in the 82nd minute. The goal was ruled out because he pushed Bremer with both hands. Near the end, Vicario saved twice in quick succession to protect the point. Juventus also claimed a penalty when the ball struck João Mário’s arm in the Fiorentina area, but none was given.

Referee Andrea Colombo booked three Juventus players. Juan Cabal was cautioned in the 13th minute and Bremer in the 22nd. Kolo Muani was booked for dissent in the 73rd. Christ Inao Oulaï was Fiorentina’s only booking.

Industry observers note that juventus were without the injured Kenan Yildiz, Andrea Cambiaso, Nico González, Manuel Locatelli, Khéphren Thuram and Kamil Grabara. Weston McKennie and Zeki Çelik returned to the squad. Spalletti made three changes in the 57th minute, sending on Zhegrova for Woltemade, Alajbegovic for Boga and Celik for Cabal. Ekhator replaced McKennie in the 78th minute and Gatti came on for Lucumí in the 89th.

Recent findings suggest that at his press conference at the Franchi, Spalletti said he was not happy because his team does not play at a steady enough level to aim for anything important. He did praise Kolo Muani, describing him as the player everyone wanted and one he can use as a centre-forward or out wide. Shown a replay of the João Mário incident, he dodged the question and asked, smiling, for a different one.

Yang Hyun-jun is predicting that Celtic can make Europa League history by bouncing back from a dismal start in the group stage to qualify.

Since the competition was revamped by UEFA in 2024, no side have made it through to the knock-out round having lost their first three games.

With defeats to Ferencvaros, Benfica and Celta Vigo arriving in quick succession, Martin O’Neill’s men looked to be heading for an early exit.

After beating Besiktas last time out, however, they are still in with a shout when matchday five takes them to Portugal to face Torreense on Thursday.

Winger Yang, who made his first start since early September in the win over St Mirren on Saturday, feels there’s a growing belief among the players they can yet emulate last season’s feat of reaching the play-off round.

According to recent reports, ‘Can we make history? Of course,’ he noted. ‘We believe we can qualify. We are getting better all the time. You could see that against Besiktas.

Yang made his first start since early September in Celtic's victory over St Mirren on Saturday.

Martin O'Neill aims to keep Celtic's Europa League hopes alive by beating Torreense this week.

Sources indicate that ‘They are a very good team, and that has given us the belief that we can go to the next round. It’s notable to take it game-by-game, though. This is the most important one. If we can get the points we can go on from there, step-by-step.’.

It has been revealed that torreense made history last season by becoming the first second-tier team to win the Portuguese Cup and qualify for Europe. Despite right now sitting 13th in that division, they have confounded expectations by taking six points from four Europa League games.

‘We are playing against a Portuguese second division team but we have to be focused and aggressive,’ warned Yang. ‘They are higher than us in the Europa League table. They’ve already won two matches so they will be a good team.

‘We have to approach it the same way as we would playing a team like Benfica or Sporting Lisbon. We have to go there and try to win. If we play like we did against St Mirren, we can do it.’.

Meanwhile, Yang is adamant that being made exempt from military service wasn’t even on his mind as South Korea won the Asian Games this year.

Played in Japan in September and October, Yang’s side defeated the hosts 1-0 in the final.

That meant all the South Korean players were no longer obliged to spend time serving in the military before they turn 28.

Yang, 24, who suffered a hamstring injury in the opening victory against Qatar, reflected: ‘It was great. Obviously, it was nice to win it but I also got injured, which was unfortunate.

‘I was trying to be around the team, to help in any way I could.

‘It wasn’t really about the national service. Everyone was playing for the team, the country and the fans.

According to recent reports, ‘We managed to get the victory. Being exempt from national service was just a bonus, I guess.

‘The celebrations were enjoyable. It’s the first time my national team have won the Asian Games.

‘It was really hard — especially the game against Japan. It was a great achievement.’.

#95086. The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

The dachshund, a humorous icon with political symbolism

📅 30 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1173 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships.
  • Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.
  • According to recent reports, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pablo Picasso was renowned for having numerous muses — mostly women with whom he also had harmful relationships. But there's at least one of these muses who was freed from toxic romantic entanglement: a cute dachshund called Lump.

Before becoming his most famous canine model, Lump originally belonged to US photojournalist David Douglas Duncan.

According to recent reports, the dog and the photographer visited Picasso at his villa in Cannes in 1967. According to Duncan, upon their first encounter, Lump jumped right onto Picasso's lap. He apparently "decided" to stay with the painter, and they lived together for six years.

The story does not reveal how Lump's decision was communicated, but that immediate special bound was immortalized through art: Picasso painted the dachshund's portrait directly onto a ceramic dinner plate that day, and Duncan did a series of photos documenting them together while the work was created.

The plate and the photos are on show at the new exhibition "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash" held at the Kunsthalle Bremen until March 28, 2027.

Lump also appears in many of Picasso's series of paintings reinterpreting Diego Velazquez's masterwork "Las Meninas," in which the original work's large mastiff was replaced with Picasso's adoptive pet.

With their long ears and extreme length compared to their short legs, dachshunds have a silhouette that's instantly recognizable: "It's really a dog with an iconic shape, and that makes them interesting for many things" — from art to advertisement, says exhibition curator and art historian Annett Reckert.

Sources indicate that alongside Picasso, a surprising number of vital artists, including Andy Warhol, Otto Dix, David Hockney, Max Liebermann and Rosemarie Trockel, have paid tribute to the dachshund. "It's striking how often the dachshund has served as a muse, model and studio accomplice for them," Reckert tells DW.

Combined with this prolific artistic career, the dachshund can equally be explored from a historical perspective, since "there's also the fact that we associate them with something German," the curator adds.

Bred to track and chase badgers, foxes, rabbits and other burrowing animals, the dachshund originated in Germany over 300 years ago. Breed standards were established in 1879, and the German Teckel Club (DTK) — one of the oldest dog breeding organizations in Germany — was founded in 1888.

The name combines the German words "Dachs" (badger) and "Hund" (dog), literally translating to "badger dog." But Germans more commonly call them Dackel or Teckel.

Because of their long, narrow build, dachshunds are also colloquially known in English-speaking countries as wiener dogs or sausage dogs.

Beyond their role as hunting dogs, dachshunds have a surprisingly rich place in German cultural history, from bourgeois stereotype to Olympic icon.

Germany's last emperor, Kaiser Wilhelm II, was an avid dachshund enthusiast and owned several of them.

According to recent reports, two of his dogs, Wadl and Hexlsome, made history by causing a minor diplomatic incident during a visit to the estate of Archduke Franz Ferdinand, Konopiste Castle, in 1908. The dachshunds reportedly killed one of the archduke's prized golden pheasants. The attack was widely commented on in aristocratic circles, and Kaiser Wilhelm II was forced to issue a formal apology.

The pheasant incident was obviously not as consequential as another event involving Franz Ferdinand, heir to the Austro-Hungarian throne: his assassination in Sarajevo on June 28, 1914, which became the primary catalyst of World War I.

Still, the dachshund remained present throughout this global conflict. In propaganda maps and political cartoons, Germany was represented as a dachshund, the British as a bulldog and the French, a poodle.

The popularity of the dachshund in the United States plummeted during the World War I because of this association; those who owned one called their dogs "liberty hounds" instead of using the German word.

During World War II, dachshunds were used for military tasks such as mine detection.

In a recent development, however, their missions weren't as outlandish as the stories published by the UK's tabloid press relatively recently, which claimed that the Nazis aimed to build armies of talking dachshunds. The rumors followed the publication of a non-fiction book on dogs published in 2011, "Amazing Dogs: A Cabinet of Canine Curiosities," which outlined Nazi research into dogs' — including dachshunds' — intelligence and personalities.

The dachshund definitely didn't fit into the Nazis' aesthetics: "They were used in the war, too, but not in the same way as other dogs. After all, they weren't the kind of dog a Nazi would have wanted to be seen with for the sake of appearances," notes Reckert. "Take Hitler, for instance: He famously made public appearances with his German Shepherd, Blondie. They would rather be seen with a Doberman or dogs that looked big and dangerous.".

According to recent reports, the endearing potential of the dachshund is actually one of the ideas that guided Reckert in her curation of the exhibition. They "simply give the impression that they have a sense of humor," the art historian states. "That's an attribution, of course. But they really do spread good cheer and have a truly likable character.".

In the 1970s, this slightly absurd and cheerful domestic companion inspired a figure embodying a new image for West Germany: the official mascot for the 1972 Summer Olympics in Munich, Waldi.

A stark contrast to the heavy symbols that represented Germany during the Third Reich — the eagle, Germania, forests, Wagner and Prussian discipline — the mascot created by renowned graphic designer Otl Aicher and his intern, Elena Schwaiger, was as iconic as the shape of the dachshund.

It has been revealed that the designer was vehemently against including brown or any of Germany's national colors — red, black and gold — in the brand identity. Instead, he went for delicate pastel shades: "The approach to color was truly visionary," notes Reckert. "Their intention was something we are still working on today — something we still haven't completely achieved: an open, cheerful, democratic and colorful Germany.".

It has been revealed that still today, right-wing extremist groups attempt to co-opt the dachshund as a subtle nationalist fashion symbol that appears on ties or socks, inspired by accessories worn by Alexander Gauland. On the other hand, "Dachshunds Against the Right" has also emerged as a counter-protest movement.

But altogether, Reckert has focused on the dachshund as a symbol of friendliness and joy while conceiving "The Dachshund. An Icon off the Leash." The exhibition includes halls that are open to small dogs and even features artworks and performances specifically designed for them.

The feedback Reckert's been getting in the run-up to the show also aligns with this cheerful image. She notes that hardly a day goes by without something arriving in the mail related to the dachshund — whether pictures, artworks or information about dachshund-related events.

Industry observers note that "It's really crazy," she indicates, showing examples of the stuff she's received. "I've never had an exhibition that was greeted ahead of its opening in such a friendly, diverse way. It's almost a bit uncanny, really.".

  • In a recent development, juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban.
  • In a recent development, the rulings came in Official Communiqué No.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that serie A's sporting judge fined Juventus for holding up the start of the game at Fiorentina, and handed the hosts the same penalty. No Juventus player is banned, so Spalletti has a full squad for Venezia, though Bremer and Kolo Muani now have a sanction against their names.

In a recent development, juventus came out of their trip to Florence with a bill rather than a ban. Serie A sporting judge Gerardo Mastrandrea punished the club for an unjustified delay to the start of the first half at Fiorentina. The hosts were handed an identical penalty for the same hold-up.

In a recent development, the rulings came in Official Communiqué No. 60, published in Milan on 10 November 2026. Mastrandrea reached them at a meeting that day with Stefania Ginesio and AIA referees’ representative Carlo Moretti. The communiqué states that the fines, including those given to individual club members, will be charged to each club’s LCA league account.

According to recent reports, only one club paid more than Juventus. Como received the heaviest club fine of the round, €10,000, for delaying the start of the second half by about two minutes. The judge treated that as a repeated offence. Genoa were fined €4,000 and Lazio €3,000.

More important for Spalletti is what the ruling did not contain. No Juventus player was suspended. Only two players across the league were banned after round 11, according to Corriere dello Sport. They were Parma’s Ndiaye and Frosinone’s Bracaglia, each for one match.

That leaves Spalletti with a full squad for the first game after the international break. He will want every option. The match in Florence, scheduled for Sunday 8 November at 20:45, was assigned to referee Colombo, with Maresca as fourth official and Di Paolo on VAR.

It ended in a draw that left Juventus seventh on 18 points, Eurosport reported. Fiorentina stayed two points clear of the relegation zone. Spalletti noted afterwards that his side “are not consistent” and sometimes lose their way over very little.

In a recent development, the ruling did leave a mark on four first-team figures. Randal Kolo Muani, Gleison Bremer and Juan Cabal each picked up their first sanction of the season. Spalletti’s assistant Marco Domenichini did too.

Bremer and Kolo Muani are key players for the coach.

The count has only started, but it will matter as the season goes on. The fine itself is small, and the sporting picture is unchanged.

Juventus host Venezia at the Allianz Stadium on Sunday 22 November at 12:30.

It has been revealed that after a 5-1 win at San Siro, things couldn’t have got much better for Milan last night. Yet, somehow, they did. Indeed, the late kick-off on Sunday saw Atalanta host Inter and it seemed that the Nerazzurri were heading for another three points, having gone 4-2 up.

Merz draws on Germany's own reunification experience, saying division causes suffering.

Two German leaders, two parallel missions across Asia.

While President Frank-Walter Steinmeier sought to reinforce ties with China in Beijing, Chancellor Friedrich Merz toured Japan, South Korea and Singapore, promoting closer cooperation among what he calls the world's "middle powers.".

Together, the visits highlight Berlin's effort to lower risks without decoupling from China.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Germany's annual inflation rate eased to 2.8% in October from 3.3% in September, with economists pointing to the government's fuel tax cut as the main reason.

Sources indicate that preliminary figures from the Federal Statistical Office revealed energy prices rose 12.2% compared with a year earlier, down from 14.9% in September. Services inflation slowed to 2.5%, while food inflation remained at 0.4%.

"The decisive factor was the fuel tax cut," noted Silke Tober of the Macroeconomic Policy Institute. The reduction took effect in October and runs through December, although rising crude oil prices partly offset the savings at the pump.

ING bank economist Carsten Brzeski said higher energy costs had yet to feed through into broader price increases. Unlike during the 2022 energy crisis, consumers were unwilling or unable to absorb substantially higher prices, he said.

Recent findings suggest that but economists warned the relief could prove temporary. "Gas and oil prices have risen significantly again in recent weeks," noted Stephanie Schoenwald, an economist at Germany's state-owned development bank KfW, citing continuing conflicts and lower inventories.

Industry observers note that german President's Frank-Walter Steinmeier latest trip to Asia was intended to provide more clarity. Amid a delicate period, Steinmeier sought a balancing act in China between respect and criticism.

It was a state visit of a kind rarely seen today. For four days, Steinmeier traveled across the country: from Hefei, where the German automaker Volkswagen's China operations are headquartered, through historic villages and the imposing landscapes of the Yellow Mountains. He also visited several points of interest of Chinese history, art, and science, and finally, he headed to Tiananmen Square in the heart of Beijing's political center.

Steinmeier—who is set to leave office in March 2027— spoke as a statesman and diplomat on matters of German and European interest. Chinese President Xi Jinping and Steinmeier have known each other for many years, so in this respect, the president was the right man to address even the most difficult issues as a European.

This political balancing act between respect and criticism did not trigger any visible outrage in Beijing.

When he spoke with Chinese leaders about their subsidies for exports to Europe and the related issue of the trade deficit, Xi replied: "I am ready to work together to open a fresh chapter in the comprehensive strategic partnership between our two countries and to advance the development of global governance.".

Just how much willingness lies behind the push for a strategic partnership will become clear during further negotiations between the EU and China.

Xi Jinping seems to understand that a persistent trade deficit with Europe could also become a problem for his country, as an economic crisis in Europe could further strain China's economy.

As "the world's second- and third-largest economies," China and Germany also bear "an key responsibility for the development of relations between China and Europe, as well as for stable growth in the global economy," Xi Jinping said. While that may not sound like a breakthrough yet, it certainly sounds like an understanding.

In contrast to his economic arguments, Steinmeier's political appeals for Beijing to assume more responsibility for the international order fell on deaf ears.

The German president addressed global conflicts and wars on several occasions in Beijing, including Russia's war of aggression in Ukraine. But he received no responses in official statements.

That same evening, the news channel of the Chinese TV network CCTV aired a report that merely covered Steinmeier's visit to a well-known astrophysics institute.

There was no mention of the call for China, as a permanent member of the UN Security Council, to do more to promote world peace.

It has been revealed that mitat Özdemir is one of more than 870,000 Turkish workers who were recruited to Germany by a government program between 1961 and 1973. He dealt with tough factory work, language barriers and cultural differences.

Six decades later, he and his family still live in Germany. How did the program from back then shape their lives and modern Germany?

German Chancellor Friedrich Merz on Friday visited the Panmunjom truce village at the demilitarized zone (DMZ) separating North and South Korea, briefly standing on the North Korean side inside the barracks.

North and South Korea have been divided since the end of hostilities in the Korean War in 1953, with a border running across the peninsula.

In remarks to reporters, Merz recalled Germany's reunification 36 years ago.

"Let us hope that Korea too gets the chance one day to regain state unity," he mentioned.

"You can also notice it here at this place, how much a country suffers from division and how strong the desire is for reunification, at least in this part of the Korean Peninsula," he said, adding that he had been asked about Germany's reunification experience while visiting Seoul.

North Korea, however, has backed away in recent years from diplomacy with the South, having officially removed language calling for reunification from its constitution while changing the South's status to that of a "hostile state.".

A glass cabinet containing memorabilia linked to the 1958 Munich Air Disaster, in which eight Manchester United footballers lost their lives, was smashed and plundered in the Munich suburb of Trudering this week.

The display case on Manchesterplatz forms part of a memorial commemorating the tragedy which occurred when the United team made a refueling stop in Munich while on the way back from a European Cup game in Belgrade, Serbia, on February 6, 1958.

The plane struggled to take off again in the wintery conditions at the old Munich-Riem airport to the east of the city center and, on the third attempt, ploughed off the end of the runway and into a house. Of the 44 people on board, 23 were killed, including eight United players, several journalists and two crew members.

The crash site has become a place of pilgrimage for United supporters and, in 2020, the cabinet was installed on the initiative of the Red Docs Munich – a local Bayern Munich fan club – to house the various memorabilia and tributes left by visitors.

Sources indicate that munich police noted the cabinet was broken into on Monday morning between 8 a.m. and 1 p.m. local time (07:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. UTC), with the unknown perpetrators making off with a glass sculpture and several medals.

"They don't understand the damage that they've caused," Ifty Ahmed, chairman of the Manchester Munich Memorial Foundation (MMMF), told the BBC, adding: "Whatever they've taken from inside the showcase, they haven't taken our memories.".

The Red Docs Munich arranged for replacement glass to be installed on the same day. The MMMF said Manchester United had offered to pay for the repairs but said the foundation had covered the costs itself.

The joint commemoration of the 1958 disaster and the maintenance of the memorial site has produced extensive and friendly relations between Bayern Munich and Manchester United, who will meet in the Champions League in January.

German politicians have been slow to respond as they wait to see who is likely to comprise the next coalition. Many are also hoping for a government without religious hardliners.

Profits of German luxury car brand Audi for the third quarter came plunged 87% year-on-year to €95 million ($106 million), the Volkswagen subsidiary reported on Friday. This is a drop from €718 million seen in the same quarter last year.

The drop comes amid weak demand in China, and US tariffs.

"Market and competitive conditions have become significantly more difficult in the third quarter," Audi chief financial officer Jürgen Rittersberger told journalists on a call.

"That all highlights that we need to intensify measures and set clear priorities," he added.

Overall in the first nine months of 2026, Audi's profits have dropped 41% to €1.22 billion.

The carmaker trimmed its 2026 profit outlook down to 3 to 5% for the year, down from the previous 5 to 7%.

Audi's sluggish numbers represent more bad news for the 10-brand Volkswagen Group, which on Thursday reported its largest quarterly loss in more than a ‌decade, at nearly €6 billion.
